combinations.title: Ampicillin + gentamicin
combinations.body: Classic teaching pair for Enterococcus faecalis endocarditis when aminoglycoside synergy is still appropriate and high-level aminoglycoside resistance is not blocking the plan.
combinations.why: Cell-wall activity increases aminoglycoside uptake. The second drug is not there to look broad. It is there to create synergy.
combinations.caution: Renal and ototoxicity risk matter. This is not a casual add-on.

combinations.title: Ampicillin + ceftriaxone
combinations.body: High-yield trainee pair for E. faecalis endocarditis when you want to avoid aminoglycoside toxicity.
combinations.why: The teaching pearl is targeted dual beta-lactam synergy, not broad empiric coverage.
combinations.caution: This is organism-specific thinking. Do not copy it into unrelated syndromes.

combinations.title: Daptomycin + ceftaroline
combinations.body: Memorable salvage pair for persistent MRSA bacteremia and difficult VISA or VRSA-type situations.
combinations.why: Ceftaroline changes the membrane or cell-wall context and can help daptomycin perform better in selected salvage scenarios.
combinations.caution: This lives in specialist territory, especially when bacteremia is persistent.

combinations.title: Ceftriaxone + metronidazole
combinations.body: A practical teaching pair for intra-abdominal coverage when ceftriaxone alone forgot anaerobes.
combinations.why: The second drug fixes a spectrum gap. It is not a fancy synergy story.
combinations.caution: If you already chose a single agent with solid anaerobe coverage, this may be duplicate thinking.

combinations.title: Ampicillin-sulbactam + polymyxin B
combinations.body: Useful as a teaching frame for CRAB: sulbactam matters, and polymyxin exposure may be part of salvage strategies.
combinations.why: This pair reflects how CRAB often forces mechanism-based thinking instead of routine broad-spectrum defaults.
combinations.caution: Toxicity and regional susceptibility patterns matter. This is not a beginner regimen.

combinations.title: Cefiderocol + polymyxin B
combinations.body: A reserve-space pair used when XDR Gram-negative options are running out and the team wants more than one active mechanism.
combinations.why: The idea is not automatic synergy. It is risk management in an organism space with very few remaining moves.
combinations.caution: If cefiderocol is clearly active and source control is strong, combination logic still needs deliberate review rather than reflex use.

combinations.title: Piperacillin-tazobactam + vancomycin
combinations.body: Very common empiric pairing because it quickly covers MRSA plus many Gram-negatives and anaerobes.
combinations.why: This is broadening, not targeted synergy. It buys time while cultures settle the picture.
combinations.caution: Broad empiric use should narrow quickly, and nephrotoxicity concerns matter when vancomycin is involved.
